chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn ʿIsa ibn ʿUbayd, from Saʿdan ibn Muslim, from Ishaq al-Jariri, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever sits in the period between the adhan of Maghrib and the iqamah is like one struggling in his own blood in the way of Allah.

So the correct way to reconcile these reports is that if it is the beginning of the time, it is permissible for him to separate the two with a sitting; but if the time becomes constrained, one breath suffices for that.

key_terms.أَذَانِ: the call announcing the entrance of the prayer time
key_terms.أَوَّلُ الْوَقْتِ: the beginning of the prayer time
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: the second call immediately preceding the start of congregational salat
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the sunset salat and its time
key_terms.بِجَلْسَةٍ: by means of a sitting pause
key_terms.بِنَفَسٍ: with only the duration of a breath
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the cause and path of Allah

ai.seo_question: Is it recommended to sit between the adhan and iqamah of Maghrib salat?
ai.summary: This report discusses the recommended pause between the adhan and iqamah for Maghrib salat. It indicates the merit of sitting between them, while also clarifying that when time is limited, only a very brief separation is sufficient.
